newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank of Portugal chief sees 97 wage rise 3% -paper.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Portugal chief sees 97 wage rise 3% -paper.

text.p: Portuguese wage rises in 1997 must remain at around three percent so as to allow lower inflation of non-tradeable goods, Bank of Portugal governor Antonio de Sousa told a Lisbon newspaper on Tuesday.
In its 1997 budget, the government forecast consumer price inflation, which is affected by non-tradeable goods prices, of between 2.25 and 2.50 percent for the next year.

"There is no ideal figure (for salary rises) and there is no perfect correlation between inflation and non-tradeable goods but there is a strong connection between them," the governor told the daily Diario de Noticias.
"If we want (inflation) of less than three percent then salaries will probably have to rise in line with this," he said. -- Lisbon newsroom (+351-1) 3538254
